title: Starting Bigger Games
author: nepstercg
selftext:
I have been making mobile games for 8 years. Usually small games that 1 or 2 developers can finish in 3 months. 

I never touched bigger games because it needed man power for sure.

Now i see the potential of ai in gamedev. It can do the job of 10 developers if used correctly. 

So my question is this:

Did any of you started the bigger project? How did it go? 

If not, do you think it is possible now?

comments.author: gcampos
comments.body:
Not gamedev, but I used AI a lot for building an app that I spent almost 1 year working.

You can code faster (which is good), but you are not going to move as fast as you think you would because there are other bottlenecks that AI cannot solve or its bad about it.

For example, even if you \*could\* add more features relative fast, its kinda pointless until you collected enough data/feedback from the existing features.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: I mean half this sub are people creating a new MMO, and there are like a dozen people on X vibe coding an open world GTA 6 clone so it's certainly possible. But big games are still big and require more than 10 developers over extended periods of time. A 10 person team is still a fairly small indie team and it still takes years to make a "big" game with that team - and usually the game is pretty small - a 3D platformer or racing game or such. When you also have 10 humans on the job they're not all going to be working at 100% capacity. When it's just you then it's a lot harder to keep the grind going for an extended period of time, especially when you're used to smaller-scope projects. AI burn-out is getting to be more common these days. Also, the tools aren't totally there to make something super high quality, so you still have to do a lot of the work manually and that's where the job of 10 developers breaks apart. AI is a great engineer, but not a great animator or rigger or texture artist or modeler or lighter or level designer - it's still very entry level in a lot of those areas so you have to take on the brunt of the work and that's where 80-90% of your dev time will end up going.

replies.author: Ok-File-2759
replies.body: Imagine if all of us in this sub worked together to create gta 6 with AI. We’d have it finished before the official one comes out

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body: we could have it done by the end of the week

comments.author: cant-game-anymore
comments.body: The thing that takes time on big games is not building features. It’s iterating, tuning, polishing. And while AI makes somethings faster (like prototyping or tooling) the things that takes time to make good game is still a lot of manual effort.

comments.author: count023
comments.body:
I'm working on a spirutal successor for Masters of Orion and Star Trek BOTF that i've been mentally finegaling in my mind for nearly 15 years.

  
I started by creating a simple index GDD that listed main features, games i was draing inspiration from and hte way i would break the game down. Gameplay modules like combat system, or strategy or intenlligence etc.

Then in plan mode, fesh these out, determine anything tha tmight be interdependant or elements that might be shared overall like a sound or ui manager.

  
Then i work on one module at a time, update hte GDD as i go with, "here's what my module needs" and use placeholders were appropriate and then go throuhg each module, at the end, i wrangle the requirements for each module into something hsared (how is the ui manager meant to handle all the gameplay panels for instance)

  
and go from there.

  
been pretty effective so far, i'm in the process of trying to conver thtis to an LLM wiki using obsidian but i kinda got used to piles of markdowns for this project so i wont be going anywhere anytime soon. 

  
but that's the gist of it, just break it down into smaller self contained parts where boundaries naturally meet.

comments.author: GeraniumCloak
comments.body: the 10 devs on a big game are mostly artists and animators, not coders. ai writes code but that was never the bottleneck anyway

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
It is possible, especially with experience, and the will to learn the new tools. Even when using Ai, I still have to rely on prior knowledge and experience to make the tools work for me. It's the same as when photoshop or RPG maker came out into the public. Ai tools are good, but the mindful use of these tools are what make it come together.

https://i.redd.it/zdzunkjb41kh1.gif

comments.author: Motor-Master-4545
comments.body: A game can be bigger in two ways: features and content. AI can mostly do the features. I have saved about 50 years or more of gamedev effort, making stuff I would have never tried. But content is still a creative process with strategic reasoning. Even procedural generated content needs to be planned, curated, tested, then it can be boring and make the project fail.

comments.author: Studio_94
comments.body:
It is strange to me that most assumes AI's main contribution is writing code. That's not remotely how I'm using it.

I'm a one-man project, and most of my work together with AI has been designing the systems architecture, game components and technical design.

I spend a lot of time working on technical requirements, engineering, governance, methodology development.  

Then there is formalizing documentation, validation, auditing, integration planning, and production decomposition; it seems like a neverending list of everything but code.

Functionally, that lets me operate across work I'd normally expect to be divided among quite a few different design/development professionals.

I still provide the vision, judgment, domain knowledge, and final authority; AI gives me the analytical and production bandwidth to execute across all of those disciplines.

Code generation has been almost beside the point. Unless it has some intrinsic part to play such as validation of a combo sequence in a combat system. 

So meh, depends on the discipline of game design compared to the multipliers of out put.

comments.author: Maximum-Nature-5050
comments.body:
我一人開發已經3-4個月
農場守護遊戲
